# Declare Tracker

An issue tracker fast enough to triage a six-figure backlog: one flat
list, searched as you type, filtered, sorted, and grouped; issues open
IN PLACE for editing; create, bulk operations, and delete with undo; a
live statistics rail. Not one word of virtualization vocabulary appears
in this file — the list windows, recycles, measures its mixed-height
rows, and holds its viewport steady because the RUNTIME does all of
that; this source just declares rows over data.

The architecture, end to end:

- **One truth.** `db` holds the issues. Every mutation writes `db`, and
  every derivation re-runs because it READ `db` — no clock, no ticking,
  nothing anywhere keeping view-side state about data.
- **Views are derivations.** `shown` — the projected dataset the list
  renders — derives from the truth plus the view facts (filters, query,
  sort, grouping). So do the rail's counts, the workload bars, and the
  closed-per-day chart: change the data and every number moves, because
  each one is a constraint over the same truth.
- **Search is one more filter on the projection**, never a scan of
  rendered rows. The query narrows the derived dataset exactly as a
  status chip does; Enter and the search field's arrows walk the
  narrowed rows, which materialize on arrival like any others.
- **Editing is a working copy.** An open issue edits a DRAFT dataset
  bound with `<->`; Save commits the draft into the truth and closes,
  Cancel discards and closes — cancel is honest, and autosave is not
  pretended.
- **Selection holds RECORDS**, not indices: it survives sort flips,
  filter changes, and scrolling out of the window; regenerating the
  dataset is the only thing that clears it.

Scale: the shipped asset is 10,000 issues (~350 KB gzipped); the header's
scale control regenerates 10K / 100K / 1M in memory from the seeded
generator below — the same algorithm as tools/internal/gen-issues.mjs,
kept in sync by hand (the seed and the pools are the contract). Every
millisecond the rail reports is measured in this file, not asserted.

// ── script land: plain TypeScript helpers, zero reactive machinery ────────
//
// Functions declared here are callable from `{ }` constraint bodies and
// from methods; they compute, they never store. App state lives on the
// App below; record-shaped state lives in its datasets.

script {
    // mulberry32 — the seeded generator's PRNG (sync with gen-issues.mjs)
    function trkRng(seed: number) {
        let a = seed >>> 0
        return () => {
            a |= 0; a = (a + 0x6D2B79F5) | 0
            let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a)
            t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t
            return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296
        }
    }

    const TRK_VERBS = ["Fix", "Investigate", "Refactor", "Remove", "Add", "Update", "Migrate", "Document", "Optimize", "Rename", "Extract", "Restore", "Audit", "Polish", "Unify"]
    const TRK_NOUNS = ["login flow", "scroll jank", "cache layer", "search index", "settings panel", "date parsing", "focus ring", "theme tokens", "row recycling", "keyboard traversal", "undo stack", "detail panel", "column widths", "group headers", "session restore", "toolbar overflow", "empty states", "error toasts", "import pipeline", "export dialog", "onboarding tour", "billing webhook", "avatar upload", "draft autosync", "print styles", "clipboard shim", "drag preview", "context menu", "release notes", "smoke tests"]
    const TRK_TAILS = ["on Windows", "under load", "at 1M rows", "for RTL locales", "after resume", "in Safari", "on touch devices", "when offline", "with long titles", "in the grouped view", "during migration", "for new tenants", ""]
    const TRK_SENT = [
        "Reproduces reliably after the second navigation.",
        "The regression window points at last Tuesday's deploy.",
        "Customers on the annual plan are disproportionately affected.",
        "A workaround exists but it is not discoverable.",
        "Profiling shows the time is going to layout, not script.",
        "The fix likely belongs a layer lower than where the symptom shows.",
        "We should add a regression test before closing.",
        "Related reports have been merged into this issue.",
        "The design doc covers this case but the implementation drifted.",
        "Needs a decision from design before engineering can proceed.",
        "The error rate doubled after the retry logic changed.",
        "Rollback is safe; the migration is additive.",
    ]
    const TRK_LABELS = ["bug", "regression", "perf", "ux", "a11y", "docs", "infra", "mobile", "desktop", "search", "editor", "billing", "onboarding", "api", "security", "i18n", "dark-mode", "keyboard", "touch", "animation", "data", "flaky", "tech-debt", "design", "needs-repro", "blocked-upstream", "good-first", "papercut", "release", "customer"]
    const TRK_PEOPLE = ["ada", "grace", "ken", "bjarne", "tony", "radia", "lynn", "sophie", "adele", "hedy", "ruth", "donald"].map((n) => n[0].toUpperCase() + n.slice(1))
    const TRK_EPOCH = 1735689600000   // 2025-01-01 — a fixed base, no wall clock

    function trkGenerate(count: number): any[] {
        const r = trkRng(1337)
        const pick = (arr: any[]) => arr[Math.floor(r() * arr.length)]
        const issues = []
        for (let i = 1; i <= count; i++) {
            const ragged = r() < 0.03
            let title = (pick(TRK_VERBS) + " " + pick(TRK_NOUNS) + " " + pick(TRK_TAILS)).trim()
            if (r() < 0.03) title = title + " — 直す 🚧"
            if (r() < 0.01) title = title + " " + "deadbeef".repeat(12)
            const sr = r()
            const status = sr < 0.4 ? "open" : sr < 0.65 ? "in-progress" : sr < 0.75 ? "blocked" : "closed"
            const pr = r()
            const priority = pr < 0.03 ? "P0" : pr < 0.2 ? "P1" : pr < 0.7 ? "P2" : "P3"
            const nLabels = Math.floor(r() * r() * 6)
            const labels = [...new Set(Array.from({ length: nLabels }, () => pick(TRK_LABELS)))]
            const nSent = r() < 0.3 ? 0 : 1 + Math.floor(r() * r() * 6)
            const description = Array.from({ length: nSent }, () => pick(TRK_SENT)).join(" ")
            const created = TRK_EPOCH + Math.floor(r() * 500) * 86400000 + Math.floor(r() * 86400000)
            const updated = created + Math.floor(r() * r() * 120) * 86400000
            issues.push({
                id: i, title, description, status, priority, labels,
                assignee: ragged || r() < 0.12 ? null : pick(TRK_PEOPLE),
                created, updated,
                closedAt: status === "closed" ? updated : null,
                comments: Math.floor(r() * r() * 40),
            })
        }
        // Recency: a real tracker's activity clusters near the present, so
        // a second seeded stream pulls ~30% of issues' `updated` into the
        // last 90 days of dataset time (closedAt follows for closed ones).
        // Two independent streams keep each one's draws stable on its own.
        const r2 = trkRng(4242)
        const horizon = issues.reduce((m, it) => Math.max(m, (it as any).updated), 0)
        for (const it of issues) {
            if (r2() < 0.3) {
                const u = horizon - Math.floor(r2() * r2() * 90) * 86400000 - Math.floor(r2() * 86400000)
                ;(it as any).updated = Math.max((it as any).created, u)
                if (("" + (it as any).status) == "closed") (it as any).closedAt = (it as any).updated
            }
        }
        return issues
    }

    // the measurement clock — `[ ]` attribute values have no globals, so
    // the wall-clock read lives here in script land
    function trkNow(): number { return performance.now() }

    const TRK_MONTHS = ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"]
    function trkDate(ts: number): string {
        const d = new Date(ts)
        return TRK_MONTHS[d.getMonth()] + " " + d.getDate()
    }

    // ── the app's palette: every color that is not a theme token, named ──
    const TRK_GREEN = 0x45A557    // open
    const TRK_BLUE = 0x4C6FE7     // in progress
    const TRK_RED = 0xE5484D      // blocked · urgent · destructive
    const TRK_GRAY = 0x9A9DA5     // closed
    const TRK_AMBER = 0xB88024    // high priority
    const TRK_SLATE = 0x7C8698    // medium priority
    const TRK_MIST = 0xAAB4BE     // low priority
    const TRK_TEAL = 0x37B6A9     // the brand gradient's far stop
    const TRK_WHITE = 0xFFFFFF    // glyphs cut into filled shapes

    function trkStatusColor(s: string): number {
        return s === "open" ? TRK_GREEN : s === "in-progress" ? TRK_BLUE : s === "blocked" ? TRK_RED : TRK_GRAY
    }
    function trkPrioColor(p: string): number {
        return p === "P0" ? TRK_RED : p === "P1" ? TRK_AMBER : p === "P2" ? TRK_SLATE : TRK_MIST
    }
    function trkRed(): number { return TRK_RED }
    function trkTeal(): number { return TRK_TEAL }
    function trkWhite(): number { return TRK_WHITE }

    // avatars and label dots color by NAME — a stable hash into a small
    // palette of muted tones that hold white initials in both themes
    const TRK_HUES = [0x6C7BD9, 0x4FA3A5, 0xC97B63, 0x8E6BC1, 0x5B9E5E, 0xC06A8C, 0x557FB8, 0xB08A4F]
    function trkHue(name: string): number {
        let h = 0
        for (let i = 0; i < name.length; i++) h = (h * 31 + name.charCodeAt(i)) | 0
        return TRK_HUES[Math.abs(h) % TRK_HUES.length]
    }
    // BASELINES. `y = center` centers a Text's INK BAND — cap top to
    // baseline — so a centered line's baseline lands at (boxHeight + cap)/2.
    // Two centered texts of different sizes therefore do NOT share a
    // baseline: the smaller one rides higher by half the cap difference.
    // `trkBaselineNudge` is that correction, in terms of the cap-height
    // fraction of the em (SF, Inter and Roboto all sit within a hair of
    // 0.72). Same-sized labels need none of this — they share a baseline by
    // construction once their boxes are the same height, which is why the
    // footer gives every control one row height. Lands within half a pixel.
    const TRK_CAP_RATIO = 0.72
    function trkBaselineNudge(refPx: number, ownPx: number): number {
        return Math.round(TRK_CAP_RATIO * (refPx - ownPx) / 2 * 10) / 10
    }

    function trkStatusLabel(s: string): string {
        return s === "open" ? "Open" : s === "in-progress" ? "In Progress" : s === "blocked" ? "Blocked" : "Closed"
    }
    function trkInitials(name: string): string {
        const parts = name.split(/[\s._-]+/).filter((x) => x.length > 0)
        if (parts.length === 0) return "?"
        if (parts.length === 1) return parts[0].slice(0, 2).toUpperCase()
        return (parts[0][0] + parts[1][0]).toUpperCase()
    }
    }


// ── small pieces: the tracker's ICON VOCABULARY ───────────────────────────
//
// One glance, no reading: status is a RING (hollow = open, dotted =
// in progress, filled = blocked, checked = done), priority is a BAR
// TRIO, a person is an AVATAR. Text codes ("P2", "in-progress") retreat
// to the places prose belongs — menus and the detail panel.

class StatusIcon extends View [ width = 14, height = 14,
    s: string = "open",
    ring: View [ x = 0, y = 0, width = 14, height = 14, cornerRadius = 7,
        fill = { s == "blocked" || s == "closed" ? trkStatusColor(classroot.s) : null },
        stroke = { stroke(1.5, trkStatusColor(classroot.s)) } ],
    dot: View [ visible = { s == "in-progress" }, x = 4.5, y = 4.5, width = 5, height = 5, cornerRadius = 2.5,
        fill = { trkStatusColor(classroot.s) } ],
    chk: Text [ visible = { s == "closed" }, x = 3, y = 1.5, fontSize = 8.5, fontWeight = bold, wrap = false,
        textColor = { trkWhite() }, text = "✓" ],
    bang: Text [ visible = { s == "blocked" }, x = 5.5, y = 1, fontSize = 9, fontWeight = bold, wrap = false,
        textColor = { trkWhite() }, text = "!" ]
    ]


class PrioIcon extends View [ width = 13, height = 12,
    p: string = "P3",
    tip = { p == "P0" ? "Priority · P0 Urgent" : p == "P1" ? "Priority · P1 High" : p == "P2" ? "Priority · P2 Medium" : "Priority · P3 Low" },
    lit: number = { p == "P0" || p == "P1" ? 3 : p == "P2" ? 2 : 1 },
    tone: number = { p == "P0" ? trkRed() : 0 },
    b1: View [ x = 0, y = 7, width = 3, height = 5, cornerRadius = 1,
        fill = { classroot.tone != 0 ? classroot.tone : theme.textMuted } ],
    b2: View [ x = 5, y = 4, width = 3, height = 8, cornerRadius = 1,
        fill = { classroot.lit >= 2 ? (classroot.tone != 0 ? classroot.tone : theme.textMuted) : theme.line } ],
    b3: View [ x = 10, y = 0, width = 3, height = 12, cornerRadius = 1,
        fill = { classroot.lit >= 3 ? (classroot.tone != 0 ? classroot.tone : theme.textMuted) : theme.line } ]
    ]


class Avatar extends View [ width = 22, height = 22, cornerRadius = 11,
    name: string = "",
    capSize: number = 8.5,
    fill = { name == "" ? null : trkHue(name) },
    stroke = { name == "" ? stroke(1, theme.line) : null },
    cap: Text [ x = 0, y = center, textAlign = center, fontWeight = semibold, wrap = false,
        width = { parent.width },
        fontSize = { classroot.capSize },
        letterSpacing = 0.3,
        textColor = { classroot.name == "" ? theme.textFaint : trkWhite() },
        text = { classroot.name == "" ? "—" : trkInitials(classroot.name) } ]
    ]


// a label pill: a color-keyed dot and the name, outline-quiet

class Tag extends View [ height = 18, cornerRadius = 9,
    t: string = "",
    width = { this.cap.width + 26 },
    stroke = { stroke(1, theme.line) },
    dot: View [ x = 7, y = 6, width = 6, height = 6, cornerRadius = 3, fill = { trkHue(t) } ],
    cap: Text [ x = 17, y = 2.5, fontSize = 10.5, wrap = false,
        textColor = { theme.textMuted }, text = { t } ]
    ]


// a FILTER CHIP: one value of one facet, its live count, and the on state —
// clicking toggles the facet (a Control: tab stop, Space/Enter, the ring)

class Chip extends Control [ height = 28, cornerRadius = 8,
    facet: string = "",         // "status" | "assignee" | "label"
    value: string = "",
    count: number = -1,         // -1 hides the count
    on: boolean = false,
    width = { this.row.contentWidth + 24 },
    fill = { on ? theme.controlActive : hot ? theme.control : null },

    // the tally is a SPRUNG NUMBER — `Spring [ attribute = … ]` animates any
    // slot, data included, so a bulk move rolls the counts over instead of
    // snapping them. One declaration; no other wiring anywhere.

    anim: number = 0,
    Spring [ attribute = anim, to = { count < 0 ? 0 : count }, stiffness = 170, damping = 26 ],

    row: View [ x = 12, y = 6,
        layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 6 ],
        dot: View [ y = 5, width = 6, height = 6, cornerRadius = 3,
            fill = { trkStatusColor(classroot.value) } ],
        cap: Text [ fontSize = 12.5, wrap = false,
            fontWeight = { classroot.on ? "semibold" : "normal" },
            textColor = { classroot.on ? theme.text : theme.textMuted },
            text = { trkStatusLabel(classroot.value) } ],
        n: Text [ y = 1, fontSize = 11, wrap = false, visible = { classroot.count >= 0 && !app.compact },
            textColor = { theme.textFaint }, text = { "" + Math.round(classroot.anim) } ]
        ],
    press() { app.toggleFilter(facet, value) },
    onClick() { if (!disabled) press() }
    ]


// the ISSUE ROW — one calm line: icons carry status and priority, the
// title is the row's single strong element, everything else recedes to
// the right (labels, the avatar, the date). Group headers are the
// taller face. The row never mentions how many of it exist.

class IssueRow extends TableRow [
    isHdr: boolean = { ("" + :kind) == "hdr" },

    exp: boolean = { !isHdr && ("" + :id) == ("" + app.expandedId) },

    // Opening and closing an issue ANIMATES — the one deliberate act in the
    // list, and the motion is what says "this row became a pane" rather than
    // "the list jumped". `targetH` is the resting height; the Spring carries
    // the row to it.
    //
    // What must NOT animate is a row REVEALED by scrolling. That is the
    // reconciler's business, not the author's: an instance presenting a record
    // it was not presenting before takes its geometry outright (Spring.arrive,
    // via replicate.ts), so an expanded row scrolled out and back returns at
    // its open height with no motion, and a recycled row never slides from the
    // departed record's geometry. Verified in materialization.test.mjs.

    targetH: number = { isHdr ? 42 : exp ? 356 : 44 },
    height = 44,
    Spring [ attribute = height, to = { targetH }, stiffness = 320, damping = 34 ],

    // ── the group header face ─────────────────────────────────────────────

    hdrRow: View [ visible = { parent.isHdr }, x = 0, y = 12, width = { parent.width }, height = 24,
        chev: Text [ x = 24, y = 4, fontSize = 9, textColor = { theme.textFaint },
            text = { app.isCollapsed("" + :status, app.groupRev) ? "▶" : "▼" } ],
        d: StatusIcon [ x = 42, y = 3, s = { "" + :status } ],
        cap: Text [ x = 64, y = 2, fontSize = 13, fontWeight = semibold, wrap = false,
            text = { trkStatusLabel("" + :status) } ],
        n: Roll [ y = 3.5, fontSize = 11.5, textColor = { theme.textFaint },
            x = { this.parent.cap.x + this.parent.cap.width + 10 },
            n = { (:count ?? 0) + 0 } ]
        ],

    // ── the issue face: a fixed column map, left to right ─────────────────
    //
    //   inset ▸ status ring ▸ priority bars ▸ title … labels ▸ avatar ▸ date
    //
    // `ind` is the grouped view's indent: rows tuck under their header so
    // every status ring hangs on one vertical line.

    ind: number = { app.groupBy == "status" ? 18 : 0 },
    colStat: number = { 24 + ind },      // the status ring's left edge
    colPrio: number = { 50 + ind },      // the priority bars'
    colTitle: number = { 76 + ind },     // the title's

    stat: StatusIcon [ visible = { !parent.isHdr }, y = 15, x = { parent.colStat }, s = { "" + :status } ],

    prio: PrioIcon [ visible = { !parent.isHdr }, y = 16, x = { parent.colPrio }, p = { "" + :priority } ],

    title: Text [ visible = { !parent.isHdr }, y = 14, fontSize = 13.5, wrap = false, clip = true,
        x = { parent.colTitle },
        width = { parent.tags.x - parent.colTitle - 16 },
        text = { "" + :title } ],

    when: Text [ visible = { !parent.isHdr }, y = 15, fontSize = 11.5, wrap = false, textAlign = right,
        x = { parent.width - 24 - 40 }, width = 40,
        textColor = { theme.textFaint },
        text = { trkDate(:updated ?? 0) } ],

    avatar: Avatar [ visible = { !parent.isHdr }, y = 11,
        x = { parent.when.x - 34 },
        name = { "" + (:assignee ?? "") } ],

    // the first two labels ride inline (slice replication); "+n" carries
    // the rest — the detail panel shows them all

    tags: View [ visible = { !parent.isHdr && !app.compact && (:labels ?? []).length > 0 }, height = 18, y = 13,
        x = { this.parent.avatar.x - 12 - this.contentWidth },
        layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 6 ],
        Tag [ datapath = :labels[0:2][], t = { "" + this.$data("") } ],
        more: Text [ y = 3, fontSize = 10.5, wrap = false, visible = { ((:labels ?? []) as any).length > 2 },
            textColor = { theme.textFaint },
            text = { "+" + (((:labels ?? []) as any).length - 2) } ]
        ],

    // selection announces itself with the accent bar, not a heavy fill

    bar: View [ visible = { !parent.isHdr && parent.selected && !parent.exp }, x = 0, y = 6, width = 3, cornerRadius = 1.5,
        height = { Math.min(parent.height, 44) - 12 },
        fill = { theme.accent } ],

    // the OPEN-IN-PLACE editor: rides below the row's own line while the
    // height spring makes room; absorbs clicks so the row doesn't toggle

    card: EditorCard [ visible = { parent.exp }, x = 12, y = 48, clip = true,
        width = { parent.width - 24 },
        height = { Math.max(0, parent.height - 56) },
        fill = { theme.surface }, cornerRadius = 10,
        stroke = { stroke(1, theme.line) },
        shadow = { shadow(0, 4, 16, 0x00000018) },
        onClick() { }
        ],

    // a header row collapses its group instead of selecting; an issue row
    // keeps TableRow's whole selection protocol and adds the context menu

    onClick() {
        if (disabled) return
        if (isHdr) { app.toggleGroup("" + :status); return }
        if (exp) { app.closeDetail(); return }
        (parent as Table).rowClick(this.rowIndex(), this.member(),
            Keys.isDown("MetaLeft") || Keys.isDown("MetaRight") || Keys.isDown("ControlLeft") || Keys.isDown("ControlRight"),
            Keys.isDown("ShiftLeft") || Keys.isDown("ShiftRight"))
        app.openDetail()
        },

    onContextMenu(e: PointerEvent) { if (!isHdr) app.rowMenu(this, e) },
    onHold(e: PointerEvent) { if (!isHdr) app.rowMenu(this, e) },

    fill = { isHdr ? theme.bg
           : selected ? theme.controlActive
           : hot ? theme.surface : null },
    stroke = { active && (parent as Table).focusVisible ? stroke(1, theme.accent) : null }
    ]


// the UNDO TOAST — one at a time, rises from the bottom, waits eight
// seconds, honors its word

// a person's avatar as a MENU ICON — created into the standard icon
// column (`iconKind`), so person rows keep the settled anatomy: check
// column, icon column, labels on one text edge

class PersonIcon extends Avatar [ width = 16, height = 16, cornerRadius = 8, capSize = 6.5,
    name = { "" + this.$data(["name"]) }
    ]


// a ROLLING NUMBER — the rail's working unit: a Spring on the value itself

class Roll extends Text [ wrap = false,
    n: number = 0,
    anim: number = 0,
    Spring [ attribute = anim, to = { n }, stiffness = 170, damping = 26 ],
    text = { Math.round(anim).toLocaleString() }
    ]


// one rail statistic: status icon or avatar, a name, a bar, a rolling count.
// The row IS a filter — clicking it toggles the facet it counts.

class RailStat extends Control [ height = 30, cornerRadius = 7,
    width = { app.railW - 40 },
    facet: string = "",
    value: string = "",
    cap: string = "",
    n: number = 0,
    peak: number = 1,
    tint: number = 0,
    hueName: string = "",
    tintUse: number = { hueName != "" ? trkHue(hueName) : tint },
    on: boolean = false,
    fill = { on ? theme.controlActive : hot ? theme.control : null },
    name: Text [ x = 30, y = center, fontSize = 12.5, wrap = false, clip = true, width = 92,
        fontWeight = { classroot.on ? "semibold" : "normal" },
        textColor = { classroot.on ? theme.text : theme.textMuted },
        text = { classroot.cap } ],
    track: View [ x = 128, y = 13, height = 4, cornerRadius = 2,
        width = { classroot.width - 128 - 54 },
        fill = { theme.control },
        fillbar: View [ x = 0, y = 0, height = 4, cornerRadius = 2,
            width = { Math.max(2, parent.width * classroot.n / Math.max(1, classroot.peak)) },
            fill = { classroot.tintUse != 0 ? classroot.tintUse : theme.accent } ]
        ],
    num: Roll [ y = center, fontSize = 12, textAlign = right, width = 44,
        x = { parent.width - 48 },
        textColor = { theme.textMuted },
        n = { classroot.n } ],
    press() { app.toggleFilter(facet, value) },
    onClick() { if (!disabled) press() }
    ]


class Toast extends View [ visible = { shown || lift > 0.02 }, height = 40, cornerRadius = 10,
    shown: boolean = false,
    msg: string = "",
    gen: number = 0,
    lift: number = 0,
    Spring [ attribute = lift, to = { shown ? 1 : 0 }, stiffness = 260, damping = 26 ],
    opacity = { lift },
    width = { this.cap.width + this.u.width + 46 },
    fill = { theme.tooltipBg },
    shadow = { shadow(0, 6, 24, 0x00000040) },
    cap: Text [ x = 16, y = center, fontSize = 12.5, wrap = false,
        textColor = { theme.tooltipText }, text = { msg } ],
    u: Control [ y = 7, height = 26, cornerRadius = 7,
        x = { parent.cap.x + parent.cap.width + 10 },
        width = { this.t.width + 18 },
        fill = { hot || down ? theme.accent : null },
        t: Text [ x = 9, y = center, fontSize = 12, fontWeight = semibold, wrap = false,
            textColor = { this.parent.hot || this.parent.down ? theme.accentText : theme.accent }, text = "Undo" ],
        press() { app.undoDelete() },
        onClick() { if (!disabled) press() }
        ],
    show(m: string) {
        msg = m
        shown = true
        this.raise()
        gen = gen + 1
        const g = gen
        setTimeout(() => { if (this.gen == g) this.shown = false }, 8000)
        },

App [ fill = { theme.bg }, textColor = { theme.text }, minWidth = 320, appName = "Declare Tracker",

    // ── the responsive facts ───────────────────────────────────────────────

    compact: boolean = { app.width < 640 },      // the bar: brand compacts, omnibox shrinks

    barH: number = 56,
    footRowH: number = 32,        // the editor footer's one row height
    footLabelPx: number = 16,     // …and its button-label size, the baseline reference
    railW: number = 300,
    railOn: boolean = { app.width >= 1100 },     // below this the rail yields to the list

    // ── the chrome facts (the flagship family conventions) ─────────────────

    themeMode: string = "auto",
    darkUI: boolean = { themeMode == "dark" || (themeMode == "auto" && app.dark) },
    theme = { app.darkUI ? Themes.sanFrancisco(true) : Themes.sanFrancisco(false) },

    // ── THE TRUTH ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    //
    // `db` holds the issues, and that is the whole of it: a verb writes db and
    // every projection that read db re-runs. Nothing else anywhere holds data.
    //
    // This used to hang off a `rev` counter every verb bumped, threaded through
    // nine method parameters, on the stated grounds that "a method's reads are
    // not tracked — the ARGUMENTS are the wiring". That reason was FALSE: the
    // compiler reads through method bodies (declare.md §5), and a method here
    // wires `this.root.db.read(["issues"])` with no help. What the clock was
    // really covering for is one line — `issuesOf` used to read
    // `db.value.issues`, a raw property walk off the value with no cell to
    // subscribe to, so the projection never woke. `read([…])` is the region
    // read the language tracks. One spelling, and the clock was redundant.

    db: Dataset { { "issues": [] } },

    src: DataSource [ url = "issues.json" ],

    booted: boolean = false,
    loadMs: number = 0,
    adoptMs: number = 0,

    onInit() {
        const t0 = trkNow()
        src.fetch().then(() => {
            const t1 = trkNow()
            this.adopt(this.src.value != null ? this.src.value.issues : [])
            this.loadMs = Math.round(t1 - t0)
            this.adoptMs = Math.round(trkNow() - t1)
            this.booted = true
            })
        },

    adopt(issues: array) {
        for (const it of issues as any) {
            }
        db.set(["issues"], issues)
        this.takeSelection(null)
        this.closeDetail()
        },

    regenerate(count: number) {
        const t0 = trkNow()
        const issues = trkGenerate(count)
        const t1 = trkNow()
        this.adopt(issues)
        this.loadMs = Math.round(t1 - t0)
        this.adoptMs = Math.round(trkNow() - t1)
        },

    // ── the view facts ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    sortOn: string = "updated",
    sortDir: string = "desc",
    groupBy: string = "none",                    // none | status
    fStatus: string = "",                        // "" = no filter
    fAssignee: string = "",
    fLabel: string = "",

    // A filter, sort, or grouping change is a NEW arrangement, not an edit
    // to the old one — the list starts it at the top. The runtime pins the
    // viewport to its anchor row across DATA changes (so an edit never
    // yanks the reader); a rearrangement is the one case where that
    // stability is wrong, so the reset is written twice: once now, and
    // once after the new projection has settled under the anchor logic.

    rearranged() {
        this.list.scrollY = 0
        setTimeout(() => { this.list.scrollY = 0 }, 0)
        },

    // Is the keyboard currently owned by a text field? A bare-character
    // shortcut must never steal a keystroke from one. `placeholder` is
    // declared by TextInput alone, so its presence identifies an editor
    // without the App needing to know where every field in the tree is.

    typing() -> boolean {
        const f = Focus.getFocus()
        return f != null && (f as any).placeholder !== undefined
        },

    clearAll() {
        fStatus = ""; fAssignee = ""; fLabel = ""; query = ""
        this.bar.omni.text = ""
        this.rearranged()
        },

    toggleFilter(facet: string, value: string) {
        if (facet == "status") fStatus = fStatus == value ? "" : value
        else if (facet == "assignee") fAssignee = fAssignee == value ? "" : value
        else if (facet == "label") fLabel = fLabel == value ? "" : value
        this.rearranged()
        },

    setSort(field: string) {
        if (sortOn != field) { sortOn = field; sortDir = field == "title" ? "asc" : "desc" }
        this.rearranged()
        },

    toggleSortDir() {
        sortDir = sortDir == "desc" ? "asc" : "desc"
        this.rearranged()
        },

    // collapsed groups — a plain array behind a change clock. This clock is
    // REAL, unlike the data one that used to sit above: `_collapsed` is an
    // ordinary JS array stashed on the instance, not a reactive slot, so
    // nothing can notice it change and something has to say so. The honest fix
    // is to make it a slot; until then the counter is doing actual work.

    groupRev: number = 0,
    collapsedSet() -> array { return (this as any)._collapsed ?? ((this as any)._collapsed = []) },
    isCollapsed(s: string, g: number) -> boolean { return this.collapsedSet().includes(s) },
    toggleGroup(s: string) {
        const c = this.collapsedSet()
        const i = c.indexOf(s)
        if (i < 0) c.push(s); else c.splice(i, 1)
        groupRev = groupRev + 1
        },

    // ── THE PROJECTION — the one derived dataset the list renders.
    //    filter → sort → (group); group headers are records too ({ kind:
    //    "hdr" }) — non-uniform rows are just rows.
    //
    //    The arguments are the VIEW FACTS, and they are arguments because that
    //    reads well, not because the wiring needs them: the body could read
    //    `app.query` directly and wire identically. The DATA is not among them
    //    — `project` reaches it through `issuesOf`, and the compiler follows
    //    the call. ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    shown: Dataset [ contents = { app.project(app.fStatus, app.fAssignee, app.fLabel, app.query, app.sortOn, app.sortDir, app.groupBy, app.groupRev) } ],

    issuesOf() -> array { return db.read(["issues"]) ?? [] },

    project(byStatus: string, byAssignee: string, byLabel: string, query: string, sortOn: string, sortDir: string, grouping: string, groupClock: number) -> object {
        let rows = this.issuesOf()
        if (byStatus != "" || byAssignee != "" || byLabel != "") {
            rows = rows.filter((it) =>
                (byStatus == "" || (it as any).status == byStatus) &&
                (byAssignee == "" || (it as any).assignee == byAssignee) &&
                (byLabel == "" || (((it as any).labels ?? []) as any).includes(byLabel)))
            }
        // the query NARROWS like any other filter (a tracker searches by
        // hiding what doesn't match, not by bolding what does); the scan is
        // timed and the number rides out with the value — pure, no clocks
        let searchMs = 0
        if (query.trim() != "") {
            const t0 = trkNow()
            const needle = query.trim().toLowerCase()
            const hay = ((this as any)._hay ??= new WeakMap())
            rows = rows.filter((it) => {
                let h = hay.get(it)
                if (h == null || (h as any).u != (it as any).updated) {
                    h = ({ u: (it as any).updated, s: ((it as any).title + "\n" + ((it as any).description ?? "") + "\n" + (((it as any).labels ?? []) as any).join(" ") + "\n" + ((it as any).assignee ?? "")).toLowerCase() })
                    hay.set(it, h)
                    }
                return (h as any).s.includes(needle)
                })
            searchMs = Math.max(0, Math.round((trkNow() - t0) * 10) / 10)
            }
        // Every comparator is ASCENDING — least-interesting first: oldest,
        // lowest priority, A→Z. `desc` then reverses, uniformly, with no key
        // carrying a special case (so a new sort field inherits the rule).
        const RANK = ({ P0: 3, P1: 2, P2: 1, P3: 0 })
        const asc = sortOn == "priority" ? (a, b) => (RANK as any)[(a as any).priority] - (RANK as any)[(b as any).priority] || (a as any).updated - (b as any).updated
            : sortOn == "title" ? (a, b) => ((a as any).title < (b as any).title ? -1 : (a as any).title > (b as any).title ? 1 : 0)
            : (a, b) => (a as any).updated - (b as any).updated
        rows = [...rows].sort(sortDir == "desc" ? (a, b) => asc(b, a) : asc)
        if (grouping != "status") return ({ rows: rows, total: rows.length, searchMs: searchMs })
        const order = ["open", "in-progress", "blocked", "closed"]
        const collapsed = this.collapsedSet()
        const out = []
        for (const st of order) {
            const members = rows.filter((it) => (it as any).status == st)
            if (members.length == 0) continue
            out.push(({ kind: "hdr", id: "hdr:" + st, status: st, count: members.length }))
            if (!collapsed.includes(st)) out.push(...members)
            }
        return ({ rows: out, total: rows.length, searchMs: searchMs })
        },

    counts: object = { app.countStatuses() },

    closedSeries: Dataset [ contents = { app.closedPerDay() } ],
    closedPerDay() -> object {
        const DAY = 86400000
        let maxU = 0
        const issues = this.issuesOf()
        for (const it of issues) if (((it as any).updated ?? 0) > maxU) maxU = (it as any).updated
        const today = Math.floor(maxU / DAY)
        const days = new Array(14).fill(0)
        for (const it of issues) {
            const c = (it as any).closedAt
            if (c == null) continue
            const d = today - Math.floor(c / DAY)
            if (d >= 0 && d < 14) days[13 - d] = days[13 - d] + 1
            }
        return ({ days: days, peak: Math.max(1, ...days) })
        },
    countStatuses() -> object {
        const c = ({ open: 0, "in-progress": 0, blocked: 0, closed: 0 })
        for (const it of this.issuesOf()) (c as any)[(it as any).status] = ((c as any)[(it as any).status] ?? 0) + 1
        return c

    shownTotal: number = { (app.shown.value.total ?? 0) },

    workload: Dataset [ contents = { app.workloadOf() } ],
    workloadOf() -> object {
        const m = new Map()
        let un = 0
        for (const it of this.issuesOf()) {
            if (("" + (it as any).status) == "closed") continue
            const a = (it as any).assignee
            if (a == null) un = un + 1
            else m.set(a, (m.get(a) ?? 0) + 1)
            }
        const top = [...m.entries()].sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]).slice(0, 6)
        const peak = Math.max(1, un, ...top.map((e) => e[1]))
        // peak rides ON EACH ROW (a row's cursor sees its own record, not
        // the root) — the view-model fact lands where the view reads it
        const rows = top.map((e) => ({ name: e[0], n: e[1], peak: peak }))
        return ({ rows: [...rows, ({ name: "", n: un, peak: peak })] })

    // ── SEARCH — one more filter on the projection: the query NARROWS the
    //    list (typing hides the non-matches; clearing restores). Enter and
    //    the omnibox arrows walk the narrowed rows; Enter opens the walked
    //    row's detail. ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    query: string = "",

    stepHit(d: number) {

        if (rows.length == 0) return

        if (j < 0 || j >= rows.length) return
        this.takeSelection([rows[j]])
        this.list.showRow(j)
        this.list.activeIndex = j
        this.list.active = rows[j]

    enterHit() {
        if (this.selected == null) this.stepHit(1)

    // ── SELECTION — held on the App, as RECORDS ───────────────────────────
    //
    // The Table's selection binds down to these slots, and every verb that
    // needs "what is selected" reads them here — so selection survives any
    // re-projection, because a record is the same record however the list
    // is currently arranged.

        // it, so the draft has to move with it or the open row shows another
        // issue's fields. (It did, before this: only click/Enter reseeded, so
        // arrowing left the first issue's text in every row you opened after.)
        // NOTE — an in-flight edit is discarded here, and equally when you open
        // a different issue. That is a real gap, not a decision: the draft is
        // one slot, so there is nowhere to keep an edit you have navigated away
        // from. Fixing it means a draft PER ISSUE (or a dirty guard), which is

    // ── THE DETAIL DRAFT — a working copy; Save commits, Cancel is honest ──

    draft: Dataset { { "it": null } },

    creating: boolean = false,

    // goes through here, which is the whole point: the draft must follow the
    // expanded row or the editor shows one issue's fields inside another
    // issue's row. (It did. Arrow travel moved the selection and the expansion

    // first issue's text sitting in every row you opened after it.)

    seedDraft() {

    newIssue() {

        },

    // best effort: once the card has sprung open, scroll so its full extent
    // sits inside the pane — top-aligned when it cannot all fit

    revealOpen() {
        const rows = (this.shown.value.rows ?? [])
        const idx = rows.findIndex((r) => ("" + (r as any).id) == ("" + this.expandedId))
        if (idx < 0) return
        const inst = this.list.children.find((c) => (c as any).isTableRow && (c as any).exp)
        if (inst == null) return
        const top = (inst as any).y
        const bottom = top + (inst as any).targetH
        const viewTop = this.list.scrollY
        const viewBottom = viewTop + this.list.height
        if (bottom > viewBottom) this.list.scrollY = Math.min(top - 8, bottom - this.list.height + 8)
        else if (top < viewTop) this.list.scrollY = top - 8
        },

    draftDirty: boolean = { app.draftRev >= 0 && app.editing && app.draftDiffers(app.draftRev) },
    draftDiffers(dr: number) -> boolean {
        const d = draft.value.it
        if (d == null) return false
        if (creating) return true
        const t = this.issuesOf().find((it) => (it as any).id == (d as any).id)
        if (t == null) return true
        return (d as any).title != (t as any).title || (d as any).description != (t as any).description ||
            (d as any).status != (t as any).status || (d as any).priority != (t as any).priority ||
            (d as any).assignee != (t as any).assignee ||
            JSON.stringify((d as any).labels) != JSON.stringify((t as any).labels)
        },

    commitDraft() {
        const d = draft.value.it
        if (d == null) return
        if (creating) {
            const rec0 = ({ ...(d as any) })
            db.insert(["issues"], 0, rec0)
            const rec = this.issuesOf()[0]
            this.takeSelection([rec])
            creating = false
            editing = false
            return
            }
        const issues = this.issuesOf()
        const i = issues.findIndex((it) => (it as any).id == (d as any).id)
        if (i < 0) return
        db.set(["issues", i, "title"], (d as any).title)
        db.set(["issues", i, "description"], (d as any).description)
        db.set(["issues", i, "status"], (d as any).status)
        db.set(["issues", i, "priority"], (d as any).priority)
        db.set(["issues", i, "assignee"], (d as any).assignee)
        db.set(["issues", i, "labels"], [...((d as any).labels ?? [])])
        const up2 = ((d as any).updated ?? 0) + 1
        db.set(["issues", i, "updated"], up2)
        db.set(["issues", i, "closedAt"], ("" + (d as any).status) == "closed" ? up2 : null)

        },

    setDraftField(field: string, v: object) {

        draftRev = draftRev + 1

    //
    // Each verb writes `db` and keeps the derived display fields honest
    // (closedAt). That is all a verb does — there is nothing to notify, because
    // every projection already read `db`. Nothing else in the file mutates
    // data; everything else derives.

    // the people who actually hold work — the truth decides who is listed

    assignees() -> array {
        return [...new Set(this.issuesOf().map((it) => (it as any).assignee).filter((a) => a != null))].sort()
        },

    // No confirmation dialog: the undo toast is the safety net, and a modal
    // in front of it taxes every delete to save the rare one.

    deleteSelection() {
        if (selection == null) return
        this.performDelete()
        },

    performDelete() {
        const sel = selection ?? []
        const ids = (sel as any).map((r) => (r as any).id)
        const issues = this.issuesOf()
        const removed = []
        for (const id of ids) {
            const i = issues.findIndex((it) => (it as any).id == id)
            if (i >= 0) removed.push(({ index: i, rec: issues[i] }))
            }
        removed.sort((a, b) => (b as any).index - (a as any).index)
        for (const r of removed) db.removeAt(["issues"], (r as any).index)
        ;(this as any)._undo = removed
        this.takeSelection(null)
        this.toast.show((removed as any).length == 1 ? "Deleted 1 issue" : "Deleted " + (removed as any).length + " issues")
        },

    undoDelete() {
        const u = (this as any)._undo
        if (u == null) return
